positioning_recommendation.summary: Position FlytBase as the hardware-agnostic autonomy and remote-operations layer for docked drones at Bayernwerk's HV substations, the aerial counterpart to the 'one grid, one robot platform' model E.ON's subsidiaries already chose for ground robots. Lead with a tightly scoped pilot on a few of the ~40 Bavarian substations: routine thermal and visual missions flown remotely from a central location, with outputs fed into existing analytics and asset systems, and a parallel LBA SORA 2.5 application for BVLOS. Frame the value in E.ON's own language: efficiency and digitalisation (Polaris cost pressure, the CFO's investment discipline) plus resilience and critical-infrastructure protection (Bayernwerk's resilience project). Present the pilot as an affordable step within Bayernwerk's EUR 12 billion 2026-2030 programme.
angles: Platform consolidation: E.ON subsidiaries moved from scattered single-vendor robot pilots to one shared platform [S7]. Offer the same for aerial inspection, with one orchestration layer across docks, sites and subsidiaries.

Complement, don't compete, with ground robots: Bayernwerk's substation robot already does thermography and gauge reading [S36]. Docks add aerial thermal views of yards, busbars and lines, cover many sites at once, and do not need a robot at each substation.
Ageing assets and scarce technicians: substations built 1950s-1970s and hard-to-staff inspection crews [S36][S7]. Remote-operated docks cut drive time and let fewer engineers cover more sites.
Weather-proof cadence: Q1 2026 grid work slipped because of cold weather [S17] and helicopter inspection depends on visibility [S26]. Docked drones fly on schedule and on demand after storms.

Resilience: Bayernwerk's resilience project and the 2026 sabotage and drone-incident debate [S33][S34][S44]. Offer remote perimeter and fence checks and rapid post-incident assessment, framed as the operator's authorised and identifiable fleet.

Regulatory realism: BVLOS needs an LBA SORA 2.5 authorisation with a two to four month timeline [S31], and the LBA has approved docked BVLOS before [S32]. Propose a January pilot plan that starts compliantly and moves to BVLOS when approved.
German utility proof: reference FlytBase's EnBW autonomous drone-dock case study [S1] as a peer German energy deployment.
risks_or_objections: An incumbent robotics platform (Korial/Energy Robotics) is already at Bayernwerk and sister DSOs. Bayernwerk may see substation inspection as covered or ask for integration.
Polaris efficiency programme and possible reorganisation from spring 2027 could change stakeholders, freeze discretionary spend or centralise procurement.

Heightened drone security concerns at critical infrastructure may make security and IT/OT teams wary of permanent drones at substations. Expect requirements on data hosting, airspace and identification.
The LBA SORA 2.5 BVLOS approval (two to four months) may not fit a pilot that starts right after the January proposal.
E.ON already has 270+ trained drone pilots and established AI analytics partners (eSmart Systems). FlytBase must show value beyond what in-house manual drone teams provide.
A competitor with prior German docked BVLOS approval (Percepto) is active in this market.
